To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) clinicians can use the validated tools in this presentation to effectively evaluate and communicate with patients regarding weight loss, 2) clinicians can use guideline-based weight management programs and weight loss medications to effectively treat patients with obesity and 3) clinicians can use weight loss surgery as an option when other weight management methods have failed.

• The use of a structured weight management approach, including the use of the validated Weight Evaluation and Communication Tool (WEAT), improves the quality of weight management care in primary care.
1) The most common barriers to weight loss include lack of time, lack of support, lack of willpower, and lack of knowledge about how to lose weight and keep it off.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of effective and safe methods to help primary care providers manage obesity and its related conditions.
the development and evaluation of a weight management program for primary care settings.
the study and development of tools to support the clinician in weight management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a comprehensive approach that includes lifestyle changes, pharmacotherapy and surgery is the most effective way to treat obesity.
weight loss medications are safe and effective when used in combination with a healthy diet and exercise regimen.
weight loss in obese adults can be achieved through a variety of lifestyle interventions, including dietary changes and increased exercise.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed and validated a tool to assess patient readiness for weight management in primary health care settings and have demonstrated its utility for improving patient-clinician communication and weight loss.
the best approach to weight management in primary health care is to focus on the patient’s health goals.
we have identified a number of tools for successful weight management in primary practice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
primary care clinicians should be aware of and be able to communicate to patients about the risks and benefits of weight loss therapies.
clinicians need to be more proactive in addressing the obesity epidemic.
primary care providers should feel empowered and confident in their ability to provide evidence-based weight management to their patients.
